hints.title: Extreme Indices Identification
hints.text: Locate the index of the minimum element and the index of the maximum element.

hints.title: Three Structural Strategies
hints.text: Consider removing both from the front, removing both from the back, or removing one from each opposite end.

hints.title: Minimum Deletion Selection
hints.text: Calculate the count for each of the three candidate approaches and choose the smallest value.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
class Solution:
    def minimumDeletions(self, nums: list[int]) -> int:
        n = len(nums)
        if n <= 2:
            return n

        min_idx = nums.index(min(nums))
        max_idx = nums.index(max(nums))

        i = min(min_idx, max_idx)
        j = max(min_idx, max_idx)

        both_front = j + 1
        both_back = n - i
        one_each = (i + 1) + (n - j)

        return min(both_front, both_back, one_each)
```

complexity.time: O(N) single pass to find indices and constant math
complexity.notes: Compare three removal strategies: both from front, both from back, or one from each side.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating every possible sequence of front and back deletions takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Finding the two extreme indices in a single pass identifies the best strategy instantly.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should evaluate the three candidate deletion options using indices.
